newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech shares mixed as PX50 index edges higher.
newsitem.headline: Czech shares mixed as PX50 index edges higher.

text.p: Czech major share prices were mixed on the Prague Stock Exchange on Monday as the PX50 index edged up 0.2 points to 567.0.
SPT Telecom and Komercni Banka shares both gained ground, but the index's climb was stymied by a 4.9 percent loss to savings bank Ceska Sporitelna.
Overall, 284 issues rose, while 259 fell and 173 held steady. Total volume was average at 650,842 shares on turnover of 654.63 million crowns.
Dealers said SPT shares, which have risen by over 30 percent since the start of the year, remain a long-term buy.
"SPT trades at a P/E multiple of just over 20 times this year's earnings, indiocating a premium to the market of almost 100 percent," said Eugene Klerk, an analyst at ABN-Amro.

"Despite the premium, and the current pressure on SPT's (profit) margins, we do not feel the shares are overvalued ...The premium does, however, limit upside potential in the short-term and...we recommend the share as a long-term buy."
SPT closed at 3,390, up 20 crowns on the day.

Several utilities fared poorly at the fix, with Elektrarny Opatovice dropping 40 crowns to 4,580, Jihomaravska Energetika off 70 crowns at 2,380, and Prazska Energetika losing 29 crowns to 2,341. CEZ was unchanged at 1,040.
